# The Second Half Guide

> Smart, practical information for people roughly 55-70 navigating the financial and lifestyle transition into retirement. Every dollar amount, age threshold and deadline is checked against the agency that publishes it, and the sources are listed at the foot of each article.

Published by Edward Silva. Not financial, legal, medical or tax advice; this is a publisher, not an advisor. Figures are stated for the year named on the page and change annually.

## Medicare
- [The Medicare deadline that never forgives you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-enrollment): Almost every date in this decade is negotiable. This one isn’t — miss your enrollment window without the right coverage and you pay a surcharge every month for…
- [Open enrollment: what the 15 October window is actually for](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/open-enrollment): Your plan is allowed to change its costs, its drug list and its doctors every January. Fall is the only time most people can respond — and most don’t.
- [Advantage or Original: what actually differs](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/advantage-vs-original): Not which one you should pick — that depends on facts about you we don’t have. What each one is, how the money works, and the one decision that gets much…
- [What Medicare doesn’t cover](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-gaps): Teeth, eyes, ears — and the very large one most people don’t discover until a parent needs it. Worth knowing before you’re planning around an assumption that…
- [The Medicare help millions qualify for and never claim](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medicare-savings): Four Medicare Savings Programs help with premiums and deductibles, and a separate program helps with drug costs. The income limits are higher than most people…
- [The Medicare surcharge based on what you earned two years ago](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/irmaa): IRMAA, the Medicare surcharge set by your income from two years ago — the 2026 thresholds, why it is a cliff rather than a slope, and the form that appeals it.
- [Three nights in a hospital bed, and Medicare says you were never admitted](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/observation-status): Observation is a billing status, not a place — why three nights in a hospital bed may not count toward Medicare's three-day rule, and the appeal that opened in…
- [The six months that decide whether you can ever buy Medigap](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/medigap-window): The one-time six-month Medigap window: when it starts, what guaranteed issue means, and what insurers may ask once it closes.
- [The $2,100 drug cap: real protection, narrower than it sounds](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/drug-cap): For the first time, Part D prescription costs have a hard annual ceiling. It is a genuinely big change — and the phrase “out-of-pocket cap” is doing a lot of…
- [The free Medicare visit that isn’t a physical](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/wellness-visit): You get one every year at no cost. It is not a physical, which is the source of most of the confusion — and of most of the surprise bills.
- [The vaccine schedule nobody hands you](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/vaccine-ages): Children get a schedule on a card. Adults get nothing — despite several vaccines now starting at 50, and most of them costing nothing on Medicare.

- [The widow’s penalty](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/widows-penalty): When one spouse dies, household income falls sharply and the tax brackets narrow at the same time. It is one of the harshest bits of arithmetic in retirement,…
- [The new $6,000 senior deduction, explained](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/senior-deduction): A genuinely new tax break for people 65 and over — temporary, income-limited, and widely misdescribed as “no tax on Social Security.” Here’s what it actually…
- [The withdrawal the IRS requires, and the deadline that costs 25%](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/rmd-deadline): Required minimum distributions in 2026 — the age by birth year, the first-year trap, the 25% penalty, and the charitable route that skips the tax.
- [The property tax break you might already qualify for](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/property-tax): Most states reduce, freeze or defer property taxes once you hit a certain age. Almost none of them apply it automatically — and the age is often lower than…
- [Locked out of your Social Security account](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/social-security-login): The username and password you’ve used for years no longer work. Nothing has gone wrong — the sign-in system was replaced, and getting back in takes about…

## Fraud and safety
- [The phone call that empties bank accounts — and the one sentence that stops it](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/bank-imposter-scam): How the bank impostor call works, why it is so effective, and exactly what to do if one reaches you.
- [The five-minute rule: why scammers need you to act right now](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/five-minute-rule): Modern fraud isn’t an intelligence test. It’s an attack on your decision time — which is why one boring habit beats memorising every scam.
- [Romance scams after 55: intelligence was never the issue](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/romance-scams): The strongest ones don’t begin with a request for money. They begin with six months of someone remembering your grandchildren’s names.
- [When the scammer sends someone to your door](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/gold-courier-scam): A fast-growing fraud against older adults ends with a stranger collecting cash or gold bars from your house. The FBI logged about 725 of these in 2025, with…
- [When the voice really does sound like your grandchild](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/voice-cloning): The grandparent scam used to have one reliable flaw: the caller never sounded quite right. Voice cloning removed it. The thing that still works has nothing to…
- [Why your phone rings more in October](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/enrollment-scams): Open enrollment is the one season when unsolicited Medicare contact feels normal. That’s exactly what makes it the most profitable eight weeks of the fraud…
- [The numbers worth keeping by the phone](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/numbers): The real phone numbers for Medicare, Social Security, fraud reporting and local help — checked, and printable for the drawer.

- [Approaching 60 and beyond: what actually changes, and what doesn't](https://thesecondhalfguide.com/approaching-60): What genuinely changes as you approach 60, what does not, and the handful of deadlines worth putting on a calendar.
